column1: From a number of recent studies, it has become clear that blind people can appreciate the use of outlines and perspectives to describe the arrangement of objects and other surfaces in space.
column2: 根据最近的一些研究，已经明确了解到，盲人能够理解使用轮廓和视角来描述空间中物体及其他表面的排列方式。

column1: But pictures are more than literal representations.
column2: 但是，图片不仅仅是文字的直观呈现而已。

column1: This fact was drawn to my attention dramatically when a blind woman in one of my investigations decided on her own initiative to draw a wheel as it was spinning.
column2: 在我的一项调查中，有一位盲人女性主动尝试绘制一个正在旋转的轮子。这一事实让我印象深刻。

column1: To show this motion, she traced a curve inside the circle (Fig. 1).
column2: 为了展示这个运动，她在圆圈内画了一条曲线（见图1）

column1: I was taken aback.
column2: 我非常惊讶

column1: Lines of motion, such as the one she used, are a very recent invention in the history of illustration.
column2: 像她所使用的那种运动线条画法，其实是插画史上非常新的创意

column1: Indeed, as art scholar David Kunzle notes, Wilhelm Busch, a trend-setting nineteenth-century cartoonist, used virtually no motion lines in his popular figures until about 1877.
column2: 事实上，正如艺术学者大卫·昆兹莱所指出的，19世纪一位开创性漫画家威廉·布施在约1877年之前，其流行人物形象几乎不使用动作线条。

column1: When I asked several other blind study subjects to draw a spinning wheel, one particularly clever rendition appeared repeatedly: several subjects showed the wheel’s spokes as curved lines.
column2: 当我让其他几位失明的研究对象画一个旋转轮时，有几位受试者画出了非常有趣的图像：他们把轮子的辐条描绘成弯曲的线条。

column1: When asked about these curves, they all described them as metaphorical ways of suggesting motion.
column2: 当被问及这些曲线时，他们都将它们描述为象征性的表达方式，用以暗示某种运动。

column1: Majority rule would argue that this device somehow indicated motion very well.
column2: 多数原则认为，这种装置在表示运动方面表现得相当不错。

column1: But was it a better indicator than, say, broken or wavy lines – or any other kind of line, for that matter?
column2: 但比起断裂线或波浪线，或者其他任何类型的线条，它是否是更好的指示标志？

column1: The answer was not clear.
column2: 答案并不明确。

column1: So I decided to test whether various lines of motion were apt ways of showing movement or if they were merely idiosyncratic marks.
column2: 因此，我决定测试各种运动线条是否是表现运动的恰当方式，还是仅仅是一种特殊的符号。

column1: Moreover, I wanted to discover whether there were differences in how the blind and the sighted interpreted lines of motion.
column2: 此外，我还想了解盲人和视力正常的人在解读运动线条时是否存在差异。

column1: To search out these answers, I created raised-line drawings of five different wheels, depicting spokes with lines that curved, bent, waved, dashed and extended beyond the perimeter of the wheel.
column2: 为了寻找这些答案，我制作了五种不同轮子的示意图。在这些图中，辐条用各种线条来表示：有弯曲的、波浪形的、虚线的，还有一些线条则延伸到了轮子的边缘之外。

column1: I then asked eighteen blind volunteers to feel the wheels and assign one of the following motions to each wheel: wobbling, spinning fast, spinning steadily, jerking or braking.
column2: 我随后请了十八名盲人志愿者触摸车轮，并为每个车轮分配一种运动状态：摇晃、快速旋转、平稳旋转、突然抖动或刹车。

column1: My control group consisted of eighteen sighted undergraduates from the University of Toronto.
column2: 我的对照组由多伦多大学的18名视力正常的本科生组成。

column1: All but one of the blind subjects assigned distinctive motions to each wheel.
column2: 除了一个盲人被试外，所有被试者都为每个车轮分配了独特的动作。

column1: Most guessed that the curved spokes indicated that the wheel was spinning steadily; the wavy spokes, they thought, suggested that the wheel was wobbling; and the bent spokes were taken as a sign that the wheel was jerking.
column2: 大多数人认为，弯曲的辐条表示车轮正在稳定地旋转；波浪状的辐条则暗示车轮在晃动；而弯曲的辐条被看作是车轮突然抖动的信号。

column1: Subjects assumed that spokes extending beyond the wheel’s perimeter signified that the wheel had its brakes on and that dashed spokes indicated the wheel was spinning quickly.
column2: 受试者认为，超出车轮边缘的辐条表示车轮处于制动状态；而被虚线标记的辐条则表明车轮正在快速旋转。

column1: In addition, the favoured description for the sighted was the favoured description for the blind in every instance.
column2: 此外，对于视力正常的人来说，最常用的描述方式，实际上也是盲人一直以来所使用的描述方式。

column1: What is more, the consensus among the sighted was barely higher than that among the blind.
column2: 更值得注意的是，有视力人群的共识水平实际上与盲人几乎相同。

column1: Because motion devices are unfamiliar to the blind, the task I gave them involved some problem solving.
column2: 由于盲人对移动设备不熟悉，我给他们的任务中包含了一些需要解决的问题。

column1: Evidently, however, the blind not only figured out meanings for each line of motion, but as a group they generally came up with the same meaning at least as frequently as did sighted subjects.
column2: 然而，显然盲人受试者不仅能判断每种运动线条的含义，而且，作为一个群体，他们给出相同解读的频率，通常至少和有视力的受试者一样高。

column1: We have found that the blind understand other kinds of visual metaphors as well.
column2: 我们发现盲人也能理解其他类型的视觉隐喻。

column1: One blind woman drew a picture of a child inside a heart – choosing that symbol, she said, to show that love surrounded the child.
column2: 一位盲人女士画了一幅画，画中的孩子被描绘在一个心形的图案里。她选择这个符号，是因为希望以此表达爱意围绕着孩子身边。

column1: With Chang Hong Liu, a doctoral student from China, I have begun exploring how well blind people understand the symbolism behind shapes such as hearts that do not directly represent their meaning.
column2: 我和来自中国的博士生刘昌红一起，开始研究盲人是否能够理解那些并非直接代表特定意义的形状所蕴含的象征意义。比如，心形符号就具有这样的象征意义。

column1: We gave a list of twenty pairs of words to sighted subjects and asked them to pick from each pair the term that best related to a circle and the term that best related to a square.
column2: 我们向视力正常的受试者提供了一份包含二十对词语的列表，要求他们从每对词语中选出一个最与圆形相关的词，一个最与正方形相关的词。

column1: For example, we asked: What goes with soft?
column2: 例如，我们问：什么与‘柔软’搭配？

column1: A circle or a square?
column2: 圆形还是方形？

column1: Which shape goes with hard?
column2: 哪种形状对应‘硬’？

column1: All our subjects deemed the circle soft and the square hard.
column2: 所有受试者都认为圆形柔软，方形坚硬。

column1: A full 94% ascribed happy to the circle, instead of sad.
column2: 94%的人将‘快乐’归因于圆形，而不是悲伤。

column1: But other pairs revealed less agreement: 79% matched fast to slow and weak to strong, respectively.
column2: 但其他配对显示一致性较低：79%的受试者将快与慢、弱与强分别匹配。

column1: And only 51% linked deep to circle and shallow to square.
column2: 只有51%的受试者将深色与圆形、浅色与方形联系起来。

column1: (See Fig. 2) When we tested four totally blind volunteers using the same list, we found that their choices closely resembled those made by the sighted subjects.
column2: （见图2）在使用同一份列表对四位完全失明的志愿者进行测试时，我们发现他们的选择与视力正常者非常相似。

column1: One man, who had been blind since birth, scored extremely well.
column2: 有一个自出生就失明的人，取得了极高的分数。

column1: He made only one match differing from the consensus, assigning ‘far’ to square and ‘near’ to circle.
column2: 他与普遍观点仅有一处不同：将‘远’归为正方形，将‘近’归为圆形。

column1: In fact, only a small majority of sighted subjects – 53% – had paired far and near to the opposite partners.
column2: 实际上，只有53%的视力正常者将远近与对应的伙伴配对到了相反方向。

column1: Thus, we concluded that the blind interpret abstract shapes as sighted people do.
column2: 因此，我们得出结论：盲人对抽象形状的解读方式与视力正常的人相同。
